state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me explain the correct method, and then we will work through an example together. Can you tell me what rest and movement represent on a distance-time graph?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, I think rest means when Fido isn't moving, like when he's just standing still, and movement is when he's actually walking or running away from home. But I'm still confused about how to tell when he's resting or moving just by looking at the graph. Can you help me understand the negative slope part better?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's work through an example together to clarify the concept. Can you identify where on the graph Fido is resting and where he is in motion?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher asks generic questions about rest and movement without directly addressing why the student thinks a negative slope means 'asleep,' and the student's final turn shows no progress toward understanding that negative slopes represent movement back toward home rather than rest.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher mentions explaining the correct method and working through examples, they never actually provide the direct explanation or worked example that is central to the traditional strategy, instead only asking questions without delivering the promised instruction.
